sources.title: NASA COOLR landslide report points - India country-name query
sources.copyright: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, landslides.nasa.gov
sources.license: Publicly accessible NASA repository; retain contributor/source attribution and review linked dataset terms. No third-party GSI inventory is bundled.
sources.citation: Juang, Stanley and Kirschbaum (2019), Using citizen science to expand the global map of landslides: Introducing COOLR, PLOS ONE 14(7): e0218657. DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0218657
sources.transformations: Country-name query; point geometries only; UTC event dates; selected source attributes; point-in-polygon assignment to dated boundary snapshots.
sources.limitations: Report locations and dates can be uncertain. Coverage is incomplete and reporting-biased. Zero reports does not indicate zero hazard. Report counts are not independent event counts. No automatic de-duplication across sources is claimed.

sources.title: geoBoundaries India ADM1
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 2.5 India (CC BY 2.5 IN)
sources.original_sources: DataMeet India community, Election Commission of India
sources.citation: Runfola et al. (2020), geoBoundaries: A global database of political administrative boundaries, PLOS ONE 15(4): e0231866. DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0231866
sources.transformations: Simplified download, further simplified with 300 m tolerance in EPSG:6933, topology preserved within each feature; ADM2 parent assigned by greatest area overlap in EPSG:6933. Coordinates rounded to 4 decimals. Dated research snapshot; not survey-grade geometry.

exclusions: GSI-attributed third-party mirror and exact model training points
refresh: Manual, reproducible snapshot. Run scripts/prepare_data.py after reviewing upstream changes; remove only the desired .cache files to refetch.
boundary_notice: Snapshot geography for research, not an official or current administrative or territorial representation. State and district vintages differ. ADM2 metadata declares 736 units, while its simplified file contains 735; this discrepancy is preserved rather than filled with invented geometry.
